why: XLK set a record close $202.00 Tuesday and lost $200 Thursday on the week's heaviest volume (9.1M); Friday's bounce to $198.78 came on the lightest (5.6M) and never retook $200; -0.52 pct W/W ended a six-week run and the fund lagged SPY by 1.68 pts (wiki/tech.md; wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR ROTATION FLOW; macro/facts.json).

The AI trade's risk moved from the discount rate to the funding of demand: the FT's OpenAI revenue shortfall (~$20B under estimates) and the WSJ's Broadcom $50B+ financing landed Thursday; SMH -4.32 pct, first close under $609.66 on 11.2M shares (80 pct above its 20-day average); LRCX -8.2, AMAT -6.1, INTC -12.3 pct; all three desks want TSMC's Thursday guide and ASML's Wednesday orders before touching equipment (wiki/semiconductors.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 4 and Wire 1).

The sector split rather than exited: MSFT +3.4, PLTR +10.8, CSCO +5.5 pct with no sourced cause; XLK remains above its 20D ($194.46), 50D ($188.90) and 200D, one of four ETFs above its 50-day; posture 'hold the complex, do not add into $200' (wiki/tech.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 2).

Week RF cut 65 -> 48 and MC 45 -> 40: the leadership break is confirmed in semis and the board adds SMH $600 to its watch; the calendar-page instruction is 'do not buy the dip in anything long-duration or AI-funding-dependent before Wednesday at 8:30' (wiki/canary-watch.md COUNCIL READ; wiki/economic-calendar.md).
risks: Falsifier for the caution: XLK takes back $200 on volume and SMH reclaims $609.66 after $600.32 holds Mon-Tue; TSMC's Q4 guide and 2027 capex raise confirm equipment demand did not break on a funding story (wiki/semiconductors.md; wiki/tech.md).

A hot core CPI (> +0.3 pct) locks December and tests 5.364 pct on the 10Y -- a 1.45-beta, 32-35x fund with NVDA+AAPL at 29 pct of it; a second leg of the funding story (Oracle, AVGO) hits the platforms that were bought because the chips were sold (wiki/tech.md WILD CARD; wiki/economic-calendar.md).
Levels: close under $196.48 -> 20D $194.46 -> $190-191.75; SMH under $600.32 -> $591.92 -> $578-581 (50D plus breakout line) (wiki/synthesis.md Section 5).
Trailing P/E reads 32.5x vs 35.4x last week (SMH 32.2x vs 43.1x) on a data-basis change, not a re-rating; the pages keep the valuation argument on the old figures (wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.C).

why: XLK is still the month's leader by every arithmetic the panel computes (+9.8 pts vs SPY, breadth 80, up-volume 88.7 pct) and the only two ETFs ahead of SPY over a month are SMH (+4.94 pts) and XLK (+4.58) (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR ROTATION FLOW).

Nothing in the demand numbers got worse: TSMC's Q3 revenue (~US$46.7B) beat the top of its own guide by ~$1B, TrendForce Q4 DRAM +10-15 pct, equipment orders from the Micron capex plan stand; what changed is who pays, and 'it works as long as the lenders keep lending at a 5.6 pct long bond' (wiki/semiconductors.md Cecil; wiki/synthesis.md Section 4).

Month RF cut 60 -> 52 and MC 52 -> 50: the window carries LRCX Oct 21, TXN Oct 21, MSFT Oct 28 (FOMC day), INTC Oct 29, AAPL Nov 2, AMD Nov 3 -- the first top-ten receipts since the leadership break (wiki/tech.md EARNINGS CALENDAR; wiki/earnings-surveillance.md).
risks: Concentration: one factor no longer drives the tape but the index is still two sectors deep over a month; if the rotation of this week continues, the average stock improves while the cap-weighted index stalls (wiki/canary-watch.md MARKET BREADTH).

DXY 102.21 with Q3 translation to come (MSFT/AAPL); the 30Y at 5.60 pct against Ophelia's 5.75 pct line; a December hike priced as a schedule rather than a risk (wiki/tech.md MACRO OVERLAY; wiki/economic-calendar.md).

Falsifier: a close under the 50D ($188.90) with SMH under $578; bullish falsifier: $203.25 taken on volume with equipment (AMAT > $540, LRCX toward $347) recovering (wiki/tech.md; wiki/semiconductors.md).

extracts.lead_summary: XLK printed a record close on Tuesday ($202.00, intraday $203.25), then lost it on a chip selloff Thursday and finished the week at $198.78 (-0.5% W/W), ending a six-week run — under the $200 line it failed to hold last Friday. The week was a split screen. Semiconductors (SMH -4.3%) paid back the Micron-capex trade: LRCX -8.2%, AMAT -6.1%, INTC -12.3% on the week, MU -4.3%. Platforms and software took the money: MSFT +3.4% to within 0.5% of its 52-week high, PLTR +10.8% to a new 52-week closing high, CSCO +5.5%. The 10-year closed 5.24% after topping 5.36% Wednesday; the S&P 500 gained 0.6% Friday to 7,811.54, just short of its record, and the Nasdaq Composite closed at 27,366.17.
